title: ADWIN2: Adaptive Windowing for Learning from Time-Changing Data
inputs: A stream of real values x_1, x_2, ..., x_t (or binary 0/1) where each x_t is drawn from distribution D_t with unknown mean μ_t and variance σ_t²
outputs: 1) Current estimate μ̂_W of the mean over adaptive window W; 2) Change detection signals when distribution shifts; 3) Adaptive window length W that grows/shrinks automatically
pseudocode:
1. Initialize empty bucket list
2. For each incoming element x_t:
3.   Create new bucket with content=x_t, capacity=1
4.   Merge buckets: while there are M+1 buckets of same size 2^i:
5.     Merge two oldest into one bucket of size 2^(i+1)
6.   For each possible split W = W0 · W1 (check O(log W) splits):
7.     Compute μ̂_W0, μ̂_W1 (averages in each subwindow)
8.     Compute n0, n1 (lengths), m = 1/(1/n0 + 1/n1)
9.     Compute ε_cut = sqrt((1/(2m)) * ln(4/δ'))
10.       where δ' = δ / ln(n)
11.     If |μ̂_W0 - μ̂_W1| ≥ ε_cut:
12.       Drop oldest bucket (W0)
13.       Break
14. Output μ̂_W as estimate
key_equations: ε_cut = sqrt((1/(2m)) * ln(4n/δ)), where m = 1/(1/n0 + 1/n1) is harmonic mean
Change detected when |μ̂_W0 - μ̂_W1| ≥ ε_cut for some split W = W0 · W1
Bucket compression: merge two buckets of size 2^i into one of size 2^(i+1) when count exceeds M
Memory: O(M log(W/M)) buckets, Time: O(log W) amortized per element
evaluation_dataset: 1) Synthetic Bernoulli streams with changing probability μ_t (abrupt and gradual drift); 2) Rotating hyperplane synthetic data (d=8 dimensions); 3) Australian New South Wales Electricity Market dataset (ELEC2, 45,312 instances)
toy_dataset_suggestion: Generate 10,000 samples from Bernoulli(μ_t) where μ_t = 0.8 for t ∈ [1,5000], then abruptly changes to μ_t = 0.2 for t ∈ [5001,10000]. Alternative: linear drift from 0.8 to 0.2 over 2000 steps. For real values: Gaussian N(μ_t, 0.1) with similar drift.
key_figure_description: Figure 2 (abrupt change): X-axis is time t (0 to 3000), left Y-axis shows true μ_t (step function: 0.8 dropping to 0.4 at t=1000) and estimated μ̂_W (tracking closely), right Y-axis shows window width W (grows linearly until t=1000, shrinks sharply at change detection ~t=1010, then grows again). Key result: ADWIN2 detects change within ~10 steps and adjusts window automatically.
notes: For toy version: 1) Use M=5 buckets as in paper; 2) Skip the more complex δ' = δ/ln(n) adjustment, just use δ'=δ/n for simplicity; 3) Focus on binary/Bernoulli case first (simpler than real-valued); 4) Compare to fixed-size windows (W=32, 128, 512) to show ADWIN2 adapts better; 5) Skip the Naïve Bayes and k-means integration initially, just demonstrate the core change detection on synthetic streams; 6) For visualization, plot μ_t (true), μ̂_W (estimated), and W (window size) over time as in Figures 2-3
